reference.name: ssf
reference.note: Independent Python port of SheetJS's number-format engine. Installed from PyPI into an isolated cache; no code is vendored into this repository.

scope: Every difference between the candidate and the reference for the 247-observation corpus must be listed here with a reason and a source. An undeclared difference fails the gate; so does an entry that no longer corresponds to an observed difference.

divergences.reason: The candidate emits the section literals that surround the @ placeholder, so 1 with "pre "@ renders "pre 1". The reference drops the literals and returns the bare value text. ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.8.31 defines a format section as literals interleaved with placeholders, which is the rule the candidate follows.
divergences.reference: ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.8.31 (number format section grammar); Microsoft, "Review guidelines for customizing a number format" (the @ text placeholder).
divergences.residual_risk: Excel itself was not available in this environment, so this remains a declared divergence rather than a verified match.

divergences.reason: For a value that rounds to exactly midnight (0.999999 of a day), the candidate reports 12:00 AM and A; the reference reports 12:00 PM and P. Midnight is the start of the AM half of the day, so 12:00 PM is not a representable clock reading for it; the candidate keeps the carried value and the AM indicator.
divergences.reference: Microsoft, "Number format codes": with AM/PM the hour uses the 12-hour clock and A/AM marks midnight to noon.
divergences.residual_risk: No spreadsheet application ran; the argument is from the definition of the 12-hour clock, not from an observed Excel cell.

refused_by_candidate.reason: Excel conditions are refused rather than approximated.
Excel conditions are refused rather than approximated.
A colon between digit placeholders is ambiguous (hours:minutes, minutes:seconds or a literal); the candidate refuses instead of guessing.
More than three fractional-second digits are outside the supported precision.
Only elapsed [h], [m] and [s] brackets are defined; a mixed token is malformed.

reference_limitations: ssf is a port, not Excel: it is evidence of independent agreement, not of spreadsheet parity.
Fraction formats (R75) are excluded here: their padding differs between implementations and they are covered by their own exhaustive oracle.
The reference does not model `*` fill or `_(` width the way Excel measures them; the corpus therefore keeps both to the values where the two agree.
